parsed.explanation: Combined regime exposes travellers to tier-1 universal consequences: national passport/visa rules doubt markers and consider permanent fraud; state/province criminal facility bans include a division law reaching hospitals and private businesses with jail risk; immigration and corrections custody report birth-sex placement, hormone removal, forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. Adult-with-minor exposure is higher through school/health disclosure, care bans and facility criminalisation. No lethal penalty documented and litigation/advisories add uncertainty, but no operative protection is shown; absence of visitor enforcement does not offset enforced law and hostile practice. Thus high-risk, near severe boundary.

entry_documents.exposure: National screening ties documents to birth sex; X marker eliminated; discrepancy can trigger secondary review, refusal, additional evidence and permanent-fraud consideration if wilful misrepresentation deemed material; traveller reports include passports blocked and stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; lawsuits and legal-aid FAQ provide information; several orders challenged or enjoined; no documented operative border relief.
entry_documents.interaction: State credentials may diverge from federal passports; document mismatch can escalate into refusal, detention or fraud review.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: forced labour, guard sexual abuse, beatings, solitary; national corrections apply birth-sex/conversion measures, hormone removal, hair cuts, psychiatric substitution, reduced reporting.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented; prisoner hormone ruling exists for residents; no visitor-specific release, monitoring or consular remedy established.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Secondary screening or facility arrest can lead into custody placement by birth sex, where abuse risk rises.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal single-sex facility exclusion; state/province bans in government/private settings; one division criminalises gender-congruent facilities in government and public-facing private businesses/hospitals, first offence jail, one-year penalty disputed.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Civil-rights suit filed before effect; municipal/county ordinances reach 40% population but do not guarantee visitor access; no enforcement-changing order documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National sex definition plus state criminalisation makes any restroom/changing-room use a discovery-and-arrest event; state law applies where visitors enter.

care_services.exposure: Minors' gender-affirming care restricted, public insurance reimbursement proposed; schools/providers must disclose minors' status within three days; facility bans reach hospitals; records subpoenas; national LGBTQ youth services curtailed. Adult visitors' routine care denial not documented.
care_services.protection: September 2024 ruling permits resident trans prisoners hormone therapy; some state/province protections exist; no documented visitor care continuity or privacy protection.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or school-related encounters can out minor/parent; care denial can follow document mismatch or disclosure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders define sex binary and remove identity policies; counterterrorism strategy names pro-trans groups; funding freezes, investigations, criminal threats against teachers; arrest for restroom use shows enforcement hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2020 employment ruling and national hate-crime law remain on books; some state/province anti-discrimination/hate-crime statutes; no record they protect outed visitors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing supports facility arrests and custody treatment; rule-of-law does not offset enforced exclusion.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling with a minor: school/childcare/medical disclosure to parents within three days, minor care bans, teacher prosecutions, facility criminalisation, documents mismatch. Guardians may face denial of services or forced outing.
minors_guardians.protection: Some municipal/county ordinances and state/province protections exist; not visitor-specific; injunction/litigation not operating.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor's documents or enrolment can trigger adult screening; care-seeking or school use creates multi-actor exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence materially above general homicide identified; but official hostility and arrest precedent can invite harassment, misgendering, ejection, invasive checks.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National/state hate-crime laws and 22+ state anti-discrimination protections exist; no documented police protection for outed travellers.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response may enforce facility laws or refer to immigration custody rather than protect victims.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Pending suits, unenforced narrowing, no enforcement record against travellers, felony/misdemeanor discrepancy; uncertainty over which orders are live; legal FAQ only.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal aid FAQ, existing passports, civil-rights suit before effect, occasional court checks; no documented operative remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation delay means traveller faces current effective rules; no relief guaranteed.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar hostile criminalization and custody harm, but dossier lacks routine visitor arrests, months-long pretrial custody and illusory capital ambiguity; consequences are less certain, so above 0.15.
Comparable birth-sex custody harm and criminal presentation/facility exposure; dossier adds national screening, immigration sexual abuse and a law reaching private businesses, so slightly below 0.25.
Shared exclusion/processing denial, but 0.35-A stops at refusal/eviction without criminal jail or custody sexual violence; this regime can criminalise facility use and detain, so below 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is one system: federal document/visa rules make presentation an evidentiary problem; state and division criminal facility laws turn ordinary restroom/hospital use into arrest; if custody follows, immigration/corrections records show birth-sex placement, hormone removal, forced labour and sexual abuse. Adult-with-minor exposure compounds through school/medical disclosure, care bans and facility criminalisation. Legal challenges and partial protections are present but not shown to work for outed travellers, while absence of visitor enforcement records is not mitigation. The result is high but near-severe risk, below 0.35 anchors and somewhat below 0.25 prison-placement anchors due to imprisonment possibility, without the lethal routine custody needed for 0.15.
